discovery: Rydberg-blockade-based quantum simulation and computation with programmable arrays of individually trapped neutral atoms

nominees.name: Antoine Browaeys
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire Charles Fabry, Institut d'Optique, CNRS, Palaiseau, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum simulation and quantum information
motivation: The nominees turned the strong, long-range interaction between Rydberg atoms into a controllable resource. Lukin proposed the dipole blockade mechanism for neutral-atom quantum gates. Saffman and Browaeys demonstrated blockade between two individually trapped atoms and the first Rydberg entangling gates (2009-2010). Browaeys and Lukin then pioneered defect-free, reconfigurable optical-tweezer arrays of hundreds of atoms. These arrays have been used to observe quantum phase transitions, quantum many-body scars, topological spin liquids and correlated magnetism in synthetic Ising and XY models. Most recently, Lukin's group has demonstrated logical qubits and error-corrected algorithms. From a single blockaded atom pair, this line of work built an entirely new platform. It bridges atomic physics, condensed matter and quantum technology, and it now underpins programmable quantum simulators and one of the leading routes to fault-tolerant quantum computing worldwide.
